subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T16:00:00Z
Subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks for the conversation today — appreciate you and the team taking the time. Below is a short recap of the pain, goals, and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into a technical PoC. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

Quick summary of your pain points
- Rising token costs and unpredictable spend on OpenAI + Anthropic for customer-facing features
- Latency variability during peak traffic (affects checkout support flows)
- Vendor lock-in concerns and desire for more control over data processing & residency
- Need for consistent safety/guardrails to match current Claude/GPT behavior

Current stack (what you told us)
- Production traffic: OpenAI (GPT-4o family) + Anthropic Claude 3 for chat assistants and content moderation
- Monthly usage: ~150M tokens across customer-facing routes; peak concurrency ~120 qps
- Orchestration: in-house router that shunts critical routes to higher-SLA endpoints; uses OpenAI-compatible APIs and Anthropic adapters
- Auth/data: requests pass through your proxy; logs retained for 90 days; sensitive PII redaction pipeline in place

Success criteria for migration
- Drop per-token inferencing cost by >= 30% without regressions in quality for top 3 user journeys
- Maintain 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for inference on the critical route
- Support feature parity: streaming, function/tool-calling, and existing safety filters (redaction + classifier hooks)
- Deployment options: hosted (quick start) and private/VPC for production traffic; ability to pin model versions

Compatibility needs / technical constraints
- API compatibility with OpenAI/Anthropic call patterns (streaming + function calls) is required for minimal integration effort
- Support for model quantization and tokenization differences (we discussed potential token drift)
- KV-cache/prefix caching necessary for conversational flows to keep latency low
- Enterprise features: SOC2 evidence, DPA, data residency (US east)

Model shortlist we recommended for the PoC
- Llama 3 (recommended as drop-in for many GPT-4-like workloads)
- Mistral large / Mistral-instruct (good cost/quality tradeoff)
- RedPajama-Instruction (lighter footprint for mid-tier routes)
- Fallback: Anthropic-compatible variant for safety-sensitive routes if needed

Next steps (mutual action plan)
1) Redwood to provide a PoC plan and cost estimate by 2026-03-19 (includes test dataset, success metrics, and integration checklist) — attachment: acme-mrp-requirements.pdf
2) Acme to share a sample of de-identified traffic (1 week rolling window) and any in-house eval prompts by 2026-03-22
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff (engineering + infra) week of 2026-03-29 to scope PoC
4) Procurement to share SOW and timeline for procurement review (we can align on pricing bands for the PoC)

Attachments: acme-mrp-requirements.pdf (high-level requirements), sow-draft.docx (placeholder SOW)

Thanks — I'll follow up with the PoC plan on Friday.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

---

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T17:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks Marissa — this looks right and captures everything we discussed. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

- Token volumes: the ~150M/month figure is accurate (includes internal admin flows). Main production route (checkout assistant) is ~60% of traffic.
- Safety: we need parity with Claude's safety filters — if Redwood has a safety adapter or recommends specific classifier thresholds, please include those in the PoC plan.
- Timeline: procurement wants vendor comparisons and an initial cost estimate by 2026-03-25. Our target is to have migration plan ready before the June product launch (so ideally PoC complete by mid-April).
- Contract: Procurement copied here — they'll need a DPA and preliminary SOW. Procurement — can you share your standard timeline for reviews?

Also, we'd like to see a short write-up on how function calling and streaming will behave compared to our current OpenAI and Anthropic endpoints.

Appreciate this — looking forward to the PoC plan.

Alex
Head of Product, Acme Retail
alex.johnson@acmeretail.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T20:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Quick internal note — I'm available for the PoC kickoff week of 3/29. A couple of technical points we should confirm with Acme before we scoping: 
- Sample corpus size: do we want 1M tokens for eval or larger? For quality parity testing across long-context convos, 2-3M tokens is more robust.
- Latency targets: 95p <= 350ms — we should define cold vs warm scenarios and expected concurrency pattern.
- Model mapping: proposing we test: Llama 3 (base + instruct), Mistral-large, Mistral-instruct, RedPajama-Instruct. For safety-sensitive routes, we can keep an Anthropic-compatible model as a fallback to reduce behavioral drift.

I'll draft the PoC test plan and compatibility notes (function-calling mapping, streaming chunk sizes, tokenization differences) and attach to the PoC plan before Friday.

— Dev
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-03-16T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Marissa / Dev — thanks for the recap. Attached is a preliminary SOW (sow-draft.docx) that outlines our procurement timeline and required legal terms. Key asks up front: 

- Please provide pricing bands for PoC and production (monthly committed, reserved capacity options) by 2026-03-19.
- We require a DPA and evidence of SOC2 Type II; please include links to security docs.
- Data residency: production traffic for checkout flows must remain in US-East.

We're open to a short commercial pilot before a long-term contract — procurement will prioritize vendors who can provide both a technical PoC and enterprise legal templates quickly.

Procurement Team
Acme Retail
procurement@acmeretail.com
